title: The First Book of Kings Timeline
sub: Solomon's Wisdom and Temple · A Kingdom Torn in Two
desc: Solomon's request for wisdom over wealth builds a golden age and a temple for the LORD's name, but his foreign wives turn his heart and fracture the kingdom after his death — setting the stage for Elijah's confrontation with Ahab, Jezebel, and the prophets of Baal.

eras.label: Era One · 1 Kings 1
eras.name: The Old King and the Plot for the Throne
eras.dates: As David fades, his son Adonijah crowns himself without his father's knowledge, forcing Bathsheba and Nathan to intervene before David publicly names Solomon king in his place.

events.title: Adonijah Declares Himself King
events.detail: With David bedridden and aged, his son Adonijah — David's eldest surviving son, handsome like Absalom before him — begins acting the part of king, gathering chariots, horsemen, and the backing of Joab and Abiathar the priest, then holds a coronation feast to which he pointedly does not invite Nathan, Benaiah, or Solomon.

verses.text: “Now Adonijah, son of David and Haggith, was promoting himself, boasting, ‘I will be king!’ He managed to acquire chariots and horsemen, as well as 50 men to serve as his royal guard.”

events.title: Nathan and Bathsheba Warn the King
events.detail: Nathan the prophet coaches Bathsheba to remind David of his sworn oath that Solomon would succeed him, then arrives himself mid-conversation to confirm that Adonijah has already been proclaimed king at En Rogel while David did nothing to stop it.

verses.text: “Nathan said, ‘My master, O king, did you announce, “Adonijah will be king after me; he will sit on my throne”?’”

events.title: David's Oath Fulfilled — Solomon Anointed King
events.detail: David swears by the LORD that Solomon will reign in his place and sit on his throne, then orders Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet to anoint him at Gihon; Solomon is crowned to trumpet blasts and celebration so loud it shakes the ground.

verses.text: “The king swore an oath: ‘As certainly as the LORD [Yahweh] lives (he who has rescued me from every danger), I will keep today the oath I swore to you by the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel: “Surely Solomon your son will be king after me; he will sit in my place on my throne.”’”
“And also thus he has said the king, ‘Blessed be the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel, who today has placed a successor on my throne and allowed me to see it.’”

events.title: Adonijah Flees to the Altar
events.detail: When Adonijah's feast guests hear the commotion of Solomon's coronation, they scatter in panic; Adonijah, terrified of Solomon's retaliation, grabs the horns of the altar for sanctuary and is spared on the condition of loyal conduct.

verses.text: “Solomon said, ‘If he is a loyal subject, not a hair of his head will be harmed, but if he is found to be a traitor, he will die.’”

eras.label: Era Two · 1 Kings 2
eras.name: David's Last Charge and Solomon's Purge
eras.dates: David's dying instructions to keep the law of Moses and settle old blood debts set the terms for Solomon's opening moves as king — the execution of Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei that finally secures his throne.

events.title: David's Charge: Keep the Law of Moses
events.detail: On his deathbed, David charges Solomon to be strong, to walk in the LORD's ways and keep his statutes as written in the law of Moses, so that the dynastic promise — an unbroken line on Israel's throne — will hold.

verses.text: “Do the job the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] has assigned you by following his instructions and obeying his rules, commandments, regulations, and laws as written in the law of Moses… so that the LORD [Yahweh] will fulfill his promise to me, ‘If your descendants watch their step and live faithfully in my presence with all their heart and being, then you will not fail to have a successor on the throne of Israel.’”

events.title: Unfinished Business: Joab and Shimei
events.detail: David also instructs Solomon to deal with Joab, who murdered two army commanders in peacetime under cover of war, and with Shimei, who cursed David during Absalom's revolt — leaving both as debts for Solomon's reign to settle.

events.title: David Dies; Solomon's Throne Is Solidified
events.detail: David dies after forty years as king — seven in Hebron, thirty-three in Jerusalem — and Solomon's royal authority is firmly established on his father's throne.

verses.text: “Solomon sat on his father David's throne, and his royal authority was firmly solidified.”

events.title: Adonijah's Fatal Request
events.detail: Adonijah asks Bathsheba to request Abishag, David's former nurse, as his wife — a request Solomon reads as a renewed claim on the throne itself, and orders Benaiah to execute him for it.

verses.text: “And therefore, as certainly as the LORD [Yahweh] lives — who appointed me and made me sit on the throne of David my father, and who has made for me a house just as he spoke — this day Adonijah will be put to death.”

events.title: Abiathar Banished, Joab Executed
events.detail: Solomon strips Abiathar of the priesthood for backing Adonijah, fulfilling an old prophecy against Eli's line, and sends Benaiah to strike down Joab, who clings to the altar's horns in vain — settling the blood debt from Abner and Amasa's murders.

events.title: Shimei's Confinement and Death
events.detail: Solomon confines Shimei to Jerusalem under threat of death should he ever leave; three years later Shimei breaks the terms chasing runaway servants to Gath, and Solomon has him executed — after which "Solomon took firm control of the kingdom."

verses.text: “The king then gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada who went and executed Shimei. So Solomon took firm control of the kingdom.”

eras.label: Era Three · 1 Kings 3
eras.name: The Dream at Gibeon — Wisdom Over Wealth
eras.dates: Solomon asks God for a discerning heart rather than riches or long life, and is granted both wisdom and everything he declined to ask for — a gift immediately put on display in the case of two prostitutes and one living child.

events.title: Solomon Asks for a Discerning Heart
events.detail: At Gibeon, God appears to Solomon in a dream and offers to give him whatever he asks; Solomon, calling himself "a young man" unable to "go out and come in," requests a heart that listens so he can distinguish right from wrong — and God, pleased with the request, grants both wisdom and the wealth and honor Solomon did not ask for.

verses.text: “So give your servant a heart which listens, to judge your people and distinguish right from wrong. Otherwise no one is able to judge this great nation of yours.”

“God said to him… ‘I give to you a heart wise and understanding, that there has not been anyone like you before you and after you none will arise like you. And also that which you did not ask for I give to you — both wealth and honor.’”

events.title: The Judgment of the Two Prostitutes
events.detail: Two women who share a house and a dead infant both claim the one living child as their own; Solomon orders a sword to cut the boy in two, and the true mother's desperate plea to spare him — even at the cost of losing him — identifies her before the whole court.

verses.text: “The real mother spoke up to the king, for her motherly instincts were awakened. She said, ‘My master, give her the living child! Whatever you do, don't kill him!’”

eras.label: Era Four · 1 Kings 4:1-20
eras.name: A Golden Age — Officials, Peace, and Plenty
eras.dates: Solomon's kingdom settles into administrative order under twelve district governors, and Judah and Israel enjoy a security and abundance the narrative compares to the sand of the seashore.

events.title: Solomon's Officials and Twelve District Governors
events.detail: Solomon organizes his kingdom under named officials — priests, scribes, a recorder, a commander of the army — and twelve district governors, each responsible for supplying the royal court for one month of the year.

events.title: Judah and Israel, Happy and Secure
events.detail: The chapter closes on a single image of peace: the people of Judah and Israel as numerous as the sand on the seashore, eating, drinking, and content.

verses.text: “The people of Judah and Israel were as innumerable as the sand on the seashore; they had plenty to eat and drink and were happy.”

eras.label: Era Five · 1 Kings 5
eras.name: Wisdom Like the Sand of the Sea, and a Covenant with Tyre
eras.dates: Hebrew chapter 5 covers what most English Bibles split across the end of chapter 4 (Solomon's dominion and proverbial wisdom) and all of chapter 5 (the alliance with Hiram of Tyre that supplies the temple's cedar).

events.title: Solomon's Dominion and Daily Provisions
events.detail: Solomon rules every kingdom from the Euphrates to the border of Egypt, all paying tribute, while his royal court alone consumes tens of cors of flour and grain and dozens of head of livestock each day. (Numbered 4:21-28 in most English translations.)

events.title: Wisdom as Measureless as the Sand of the Sea
events.detail: God gives Solomon wisdom and understanding "as measureless as the sand on the seashore" — greater than all the sages of Egypt and the East — and he composes three thousand proverbs and over a thousand songs, along with treatises on plants and animals that draw visitors from every nation. (Numbered 4:29-34 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “God [Elohim] gave Solomon wisdom to Solomon and understanding very great, and breadth of heart like the sand which is on the shore of the sea.” (Numbered 4:29 in most English translations.)

events.title: Hiram of Tyre Supplies Cedar for the Temple
events.detail: Solomon sends word to Hiram, his father's old ally, proposing to build a temple to the LORD; Hiram supplies cedar and cypress from Lebanon in exchange for wheat and oil, and the two kings make a treaty — the LORD giving Solomon wisdom, as promised, in the very negotiation. (Numbered 5:1-18 in most English translations.)

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] gave wisdom to Solomon just as he had spoken to him, and it was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and they made a covenant, the two of them.” (Numbered 5:12 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Six · 1 Kings 6
eras.name: Building the House for the Name of the LORD
eras.dates: Four hundred eighty years after the exodus, in his fourth regnal year, Solomon lays the foundation of the temple — and receives a mid-construction reminder that its permanence depends on obedience, not architecture.

events.title: The Temple Takes Shape
events.detail: In the fourth year of his reign Solomon begins the temple — ninety feet long, thirty wide, forty-five high — built entirely from stones shaped at the quarry, so that no hammer or iron tool is heard on the construction site itself.

verses.text: “As the temple was being built, only stones shaped at the quarry were used; the sound of hammers, pickaxes, or any other iron tool was not heard at the temple while it was being built.”

events.title: The LORD's Conditional Promise
events.detail: Mid-construction, the LORD's message interrupts the building narrative with a warning wrapped in a promise: the temple's grandeur guarantees nothing — only obedience to his statutes will keep him dwelling among his people.

verses.text: “As for this temple you are building, if you follow my rules, observe my regulations, and obey all my commandments, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David. I will live among the Israelites and will not abandon my people Israel.”

events.title: Cedar, Gold, and Cherubim
events.detail: Solomon finishes the temple's interior in cedar and gold — the inner sanctuary plated floor to ceiling, two olive-wood cherubim with fifteen-foot wingspans guarding the Most Holy Place — completing the project after seven years, in the eleventh year of his reign.

verses.text: “In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul (the eighth month) the temple was completed in accordance with all its specifications and blueprints. It took seven years to build.”

eras.label: Era Seven · 1 Kings 7
eras.name: The Palace and the Bronze Sea
eras.dates: Solomon spends thirteen years — nearly twice as long as the temple took — on his own palace complex, then commissions Hiram the bronze craftsman to cast the temple's massive furnishings.

events.title: Solomon's Palace, Thirteen Years in the Building
events.detail: Solomon builds "The Palace of the Lebanon Forest," a throne room called the Hall of Judgment, and a residence for Pharaoh's daughter, all from the same chiseled stone and cedar as the temple, but taking thirteen years to complete.

verses.text: “Solomon took 13 years to build his palace.”

events.title: Hiram the Craftsman — Two Pillars Named
events.detail: A bronze craftsman also named Hiram, from Tyre, casts two towering bronze pillars for the temple porch, which Solomon names Jakin and Boaz.

verses.text: “He set up the pillars on the porch in front of the main hall. He erected one pillar on the right side and called it Jakin; he erected the other pillar on the left side and called it Boaz.”

events.title: The Bronze Sea and the Temple's Furnishings
events.detail: Hiram casts "The Sea," a massive bronze basin resting on twelve bronze oxen, along with ten movable stands and basins, then Solomon gathers in the gold altar, table, lampstands, and every item his father David had dedicated, storing them in the temple treasuries.

verses.text: “He also made the large bronze basin called ‘The Sea.’ It measured 15 feet from rim to rim, was circular in shape, and stood 7½ feet high.”
“‘The Sea’ stood on top of twelve bulls. Three faced northward, three westward, three southward, and three eastward.”

eras.label: Era Eight · 1 Kings 8
eras.name: The Ark Comes Home — Solomon's Prayer of Dedication
eras.dates: The ark of the covenant is carried into the finished temple, the glory of the LORD fills it as a cloud, and Solomon offers a long dedicatory prayer covering seven scenarios in which Israel — or even a foreigner — might cry out for God's help.

events.title: The Ark Enters the Temple; the Glory Fills the House
events.detail: Israel's elders and priests carry the ark of the covenant into the inner sanctuary beneath the cherubim's wings; as the priests withdraw, a cloud fills the temple so thickly that they cannot continue their service — the LORD's glory taking up residence.

verses.text: “Once the priests left the Holy Place, a cloud filled the LORD's temple. The priests could not carry out their duties because of the cloud; the LORD's glory filled his temple.”

events.title: "The LORD Has Said He Lives in Thick Darkness"
events.detail: Solomon turns to bless the assembly, acknowledging that the LORD who chose to dwell in thick darkness has now, through him, been given "a lofty temple… a place where you can live permanently" — the fulfillment of the promise made to David.

verses.text: “Then Solomon said, ‘The LORD [Yahweh] has said that he lives in thick darkness. O LORD, truly I have built a lofty temple for you, a place where you can live permanently.’”

events.title: "There Is No God Like You"
events.detail: Standing before the altar with his hands spread toward heaven, Solomon opens his prayer by declaring the LORD utterly incomparable, yet asks the impossible-sounding question of how any temple could contain the God whom even the highest heaven cannot hold.

verses.text: “He prayed: ‘O LORD [Yahweh], God [Elohim] of Israel, there is no god like you in heaven above or on earth below! You maintain covenantal loyalty to your servants who obey you with sincerity.’”
“‘God [Elohim] does not really live on the earth! Look, if the sky and the highest heaven cannot contain you, how much less this temple I have built!’”

events.title: Seven Petitions — From Neighbor's Oath to Exile's Prayer
events.detail: Solomon walks through seven scenarios — a false oath, military defeat, drought, famine or plague, the foreigner's prayer, war, and exile in a distant land — asking in each case that the LORD listen "from heaven, your dwelling place" and act, even extending the request explicitly to non-Israelites who pray toward the temple because of God's reputation.

verses.text: “Foreigners, who do not belong to your people Israel, will come from a distant land because of your reputation… Then listen from your heavenly dwelling place and answer all the prayers of the foreigners… so that all the nations of the earth will acknowledge your reputation.”

events.title: "Not One Promise Left Unfulfilled" — Fourteen Days of Feasting
events.detail: Solomon closes with a blessing declaring that not one of all the LORD's good promises through Moses has failed, prays that Israel's hearts stay wholly devoted, and dedicates the temple with peace offerings so vast the bronze altar cannot hold them all, launching a festival that lasts two full weeks.

verses.text: “Blessed be the LORD [Yahweh], who has given a resting place to his people Israel according to all that he has spoken; not one word has fallen of all his good word which he spoke by the hand of Moses his servant.”

“So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD [Yahweh], he is God [Elohim]; there is no other. And let your heart be complete with the LORD [Yahweh] our God [Elohim], to walk in his statutes and keep his commandments, as at this day.”

eras.label: Era Nine · 1 Kings 9
eras.name: The LORD Appears a Second Time
eras.dates: The LORD answers Solomon's dedication prayer directly, renewing the dynastic promise on the same conditional terms as always — and warning, in unusually specific terms, exactly what abandonment would cost.

events.title: A Warning Wrapped in a Promise
events.detail: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time, confirming the temple as his chosen dwelling and the dynasty as secure — but only on the same condition given to David: obedience. Disobedience, God warns explicitly, will mean exile and a temple reduced to a byword, so ruined that passersby will ask why the LORD did this to it.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to him, ‘I have heard your prayer and your supplication which you have sought favor before me; I have consecrated this house which you have built by putting my name there until perpetuity.’”

“I will cut off Israel from the land which I have given them, and the house which I have consecrated for my name I will send away from before me… and this house will become a heap of ruins; everyone who passes by it will be appalled.”

events.title: Cabul, Forced Labor, and Ships to Ophir
events.detail: In exchange for gold and building materials, Solomon gives Hiram twenty towns in Galilee that Hiram finds worthless, naming the region Cabul in mild protest; Solomon conscripts the surviving Canaanite peoples for forced labor and builds a fleet at Ezion Geber that sails to Ophir for gold.

verses.text: “Hiram asked, ‘Why did you give me these towns, my friend?’ He called that area the region of Cabul, a name which it has retained to this day.”

eras.label: Era Ten · 1 Kings 10
eras.name: The Queen of Sheba and Solomon's Wealth
eras.dates: A foreign queen travels to test Solomon's famous wisdom with hard questions and leaves overwhelmed, while the chapter's second half catalogs a wealth so extreme that silver becomes as common in Jerusalem as ordinary stone.

events.title: The Queen of Sheba's Visit
events.detail: The queen of Sheba arrives with a caravan of spices, gold, and gems to test Solomon with difficult questions, finds every one answered, and confesses that the reports she had heard did not tell even half the story of his wisdom and wealth.

verses.text: “May the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim] your be blessed, who has delighted in you to put you on the throne of Israel, because the LORD [Yahweh] loves Israel forever, and has appointed you to king to do justice and righteousness.”

events.title: Gold, an Ivory Throne, and Silver Like Stone
events.detail: Solomon's annual gold income reaches 666 talents; he builds a great ivory throne overlaid with gold and flanked by lion statues, and accumulates so much silver and cedar that silver becomes as common in Jerusalem as ordinary stones.

verses.text: “The king made silver as plentiful in Jerusalem as stones; cedar was as plentiful as sycamore fig trees are in the foothills.”

eras.label: Era Eleven · 1 Kings 11
eras.name: Solomon's Heart Turns, and the Kingdom Is Torn
eras.dates: The king who once asked for wisdom over wealth ends his reign with seven hundred wives who turn his heart to Astarte, Chemosh, and Milcom — and the LORD responds by promising to tear the kingdom in two.

events.title: Foreign Wives and Foreign Gods
events.detail: Solomon's seven hundred wives and three hundred concubines — expressly forbidden alliances — turn his heart from the LORD in his old age; he builds high places for Astarte, Chemosh, and Milcom, no longer "wholeheartedly devoted" as David had been.

verses.text: “From the nations which the LORD [Yahweh] had said to the people of Israel, ‘You must not go among them, and they must not go among you, for they will surely turn aside your heart after their gods [Elohim],’ to these Solomon clung, to love them.”

“And it was, at the time of Solomon's old age, his wives turned aside his heart after other gods [Elohim]; and his heart was not complete with the LORD [Yahweh] his God [Elohim], like the heart of David his father.”

events.title: The LORD's Judgment — the Kingdom Will Be Torn
events.detail: Angry that Solomon turned from him despite two direct appearances, the LORD announces he will tear the kingdom away — though not in Solomon's own lifetime, and not entirely, leaving one tribe for David's and Jerusalem's sake.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] said to Solomon, ‘Because this has been done by you, and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes which I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom from you and give it to your servant.’”

events.title: Adversaries Raised Up: Hadad and Rezon
events.detail: The LORD raises up two foreign adversaries against Solomon — Hadad the Edomite, a survivor of David's earlier campaign, and Rezon, a fugitive commander who becomes king in Damascus and remains Israel's enemy throughout Solomon's reign.

events.title: Ahijah Tears His Robe Into Twelve Pieces
events.detail: The prophet Ahijah meets Jeroboam, one of Solomon's own officials, on a lonely road, tears his new robe into twelve pieces, and hands Jeroboam ten of them as a sign that ten tribes will be torn from Solomon's son and given to him.

verses.text: “Then he told Jeroboam, ‘Take 10 pieces, for this is what the LORD God of Israel has said: “Look, I am about to tear the kingdom from Solomon's hand and I will give 10 tribes to you.”’”

events.title: Solomon's Death
events.detail: After forty years on the throne, Solomon dies and is buried in the City of David; his son Rehoboam succeeds him.

verses.text: “Solomon ruled over all Israel from Jerusalem for 40 years. Then Solomon passed away and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam replaced him as king.”

eras.label: Era Twelve · 1 Kings 12
eras.name: The Kingdom Splits
eras.dates: Rehoboam's harsh answer to Israel's elders fractures the united kingdom permanently, and Jeroboam secures his new northern throne by inventing a rival worship system centered on two golden calves.

events.title: "My Father Disciplined You With Whips; I Will Discipline You With Scorpions"
events.detail: Asked to lighten Solomon's harsh labor demands, Rehoboam rejects the elders' moderate counsel for his young friends' brutal one — a decision the narrator explicitly attributes to the LORD's own engineering of events, fulfilling Ahijah's word to Jeroboam.

verses.text: “And the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn of affairs from the LORD [Yahweh], so as to establish his word which the LORD [Yahweh] had spoken by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.”

events.title: "What Portion Do We Have in David?" — Israel Revolts
events.detail: Ten tribes reject the house of David outright and make Jeroboam king; when Rehoboam musters an army to force reunification, the prophet Shemaiah delivers a direct word from the LORD ordering Judah to stand down, since the split "has occurred from me."

verses.text: “‘This is what the LORD [Yahweh] has said: “Do not attack and make war with your brothers, the Israelites. Each of you go home. Indeed this thing has happened because of me.”’ So they obeyed the word of the LORD [Yahweh].”

events.title: Jeroboam's Golden Calves at Bethel and Dan
events.detail: Fearing that pilgrimages to Jerusalem's temple would win the people's loyalty back to Rehoboam, Jeroboam makes two golden calves, sets them at Bethel and Dan, and invents his own festival calendar and priesthood — the sin the rest of Kings will keep calling "the sin of Jeroboam."

verses.text: “After the king had consulted with his advisers, he made two golden calves. Then he said to the people, ‘It is too much trouble for you to go up to Jerusalem. Look, Israel, here are your gods [Elohim] who brought you up from the land of Egypt.’”

eras.label: Era Thirteen · 1 Kings 13
eras.name: The Man of God from Judah
eras.dates: An unnamed prophet's altar-splitting sign against Jeroboam turns into a cautionary tale of his own, when an old prophet's lie leads him to disobey the very word of the LORD he had just delivered.

events.title: The Altar at Bethel Splits; Jeroboam's Hand Withers
events.detail: A prophet from Judah cries out against Jeroboam's altar, predicting a future king named Josiah who will defile it with human bones; when Jeroboam points at him and orders his arrest, his hand stiffens and cannot be withdrawn until the prophet prays for its restoration.

verses.text: “He cried out against the altar with the LORD's [Yahweh] message, ‘O altar, altar! This is what the LORD [Yahweh] has said, “Look, a son named Josiah will be born to the Davidic dynasty. He will sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who offer sacrifices on you.”’”

events.title: The Old Prophet's Lie, and the Lion on the Road
events.detail: Under strict orders not to eat, drink, or return by the same road, the man of God is deceived by an old prophet in Bethel who falsely claims an angel countermanded the order; he eats, and a lion kills him on the road home in fulfillment of the word he had disobeyed.

verses.text: “He called out to the man of God [Elohim] who had come from Judah, ‘This is what the LORD [Yahweh] has said, “Because you have rebelled against the mouth of the LORD [Yahweh]… your corpse will not go to the grave of your ancestors.”’”

events.title: Jeroboam Does Not Change His Ways
events.detail: Despite the sign at his own altar, Jeroboam continues appointing common people as priests at the high places — the sin that the narrator says will bring his dynasty to an end.

verses.text: “This sin caused Jeroboam's dynasty to come to an end and to be destroyed from the face of the earth.”

eras.label: Era Fourteen · 1 Kings 14
eras.name: Ahijah's Prophecy Against the House of Jeroboam
eras.dates: Jeroboam sends his disguised wife to the same blind prophet who once tore his robe into twelve pieces, and receives instead a graphic sentence of total dynastic destruction — fulfilled within the chapter's own final verses.

events.title: Jeroboam's Wife Disguised Before the Blind Prophet
events.detail: When his son Abijah falls sick, Jeroboam sends his wife in disguise to consult the aged, blind Ahijah — but the LORD has already told the prophet exactly who is coming and why, so Ahijah recognizes her by her footsteps alone.

events.title: "Swept Away Like Dung" — Total Judgment on Jeroboam's House
events.detail: Ahijah pronounces total destruction on Jeroboam's dynasty for making other gods and provoking the LORD to anger — every male cut off, the family "swept away like dung," the dead left for dogs and birds — and further warns that Israel itself will one day be uprooted and scattered beyond the Euphrates for the Asherah poles Jeroboam caused them to make.

verses.text: “You have sinned more than all who came before you… therefore I am ready to bring calamity to the house of Jeroboam and I will cut off to Jeroboam every male in Israel, and I will sweep away behind the house of Jeroboam just as someone sweeps away dung until it is complete.”
“The LORD [Yahweh] will strike Israel, making it like a reed that sways in the water… and scatter them beyond the Euphrates River, because they angered the LORD [Yahweh] by making Asherah poles.”

events.title: The Boy Dies; Jeroboam Dies; Nadab Succeeds
events.detail: As Ahijah foretold, the boy dies the moment his mother crosses the threshold at home; Jeroboam himself reigns twenty-two years before dying, and his son Nadab replaces him.

events.title: Rehoboam's Reign and Shishak's Invasion
events.detail: In Judah, Rehoboam's seventeen-year reign sees the nation adopt high places, sacred pillars, and cult prostitution; in his fifth year, King Shishak of Egypt strips the temple and palace treasuries bare, and Rehoboam replaces the stolen gold shields with bronze ones.

verses.text: “He took away the treasures of the LORD's temple and of the royal palace; he took everything, including all the golden shields that Solomon had made.”

eras.label: Era Fifteen · 1 Kings 15-16
eras.name: A Chain of Kings — Judah and Israel
eras.dates: The narrative compresses into rapid royal succession on both sides of the divided kingdom — three kings of Judah measured against David's standard, and five kings of Israel measured against Jeroboam's — ending with the ascent of the most notorious of them all, Ahab.

events.title: Abijam of Judah
events.detail: Abijam reigns three years in Jerusalem, following his father's sinful practices, yet the LORD preserves the Davidic line "for David's sake," continuing to give him a lamp in Jerusalem.

events.title: Asa's Reforms and the Treaty With Ben Hadad
events.detail: Asa reigns forty-one years and does what is right — removing cult prostitutes, deposing his own grandmother for making an Asherah pole — though the high places remain; under military pressure from Baasha of Israel, Asa strips the temple treasury to buy Ben Hadad of Syria's help.

verses.text: “The high places were not eliminated, yet Asa was wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD throughout his lifetime.”

events.title: Nadab, Baasha, and Elah of Israel
events.detail: Nadab is assassinated by Baasha, who wipes out Jeroboam's entire family in fulfillment of Ahijah's word, then is himself condemned by the prophet Jehu son of Hanani for following Jeroboam's sins; Baasha's son Elah is murdered by his own chariot commander Zimri while drunk.

verses.text: “Zimri destroyed Baasha's entire family, in keeping with the LORD's message which he had spoken against Baasha through Jehu the prophet.”

events.title: Zimri's Seven Days; Omri Buys Samaria
events.detail: Zimri reigns only seven days before burning himself alive in the palace as Omri's forces besiege Tirzah; after a brief civil war with a rival claimant, Omri becomes king and purchases the hill of Samaria, founding the city that will remain Israel's capital.

verses.text: “He purchased the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver. He launched a construction project there and named the city he built after Shemer.”

events.title: Ahab Marries Jezebel and Serves Baal
events.detail: Ahab, worse than every king of Israel before him, marries Jezebel of Sidon, builds a temple to Baal in Samaria, and makes an Asherah pole; the chapter closes with Hiel of Bethel rebuilding Jericho at the cost of two sons' lives, in exact fulfillment of Joshua's centuries-old curse.

verses.text: “Ahab also made an Asherah pole; he did more to anger the LORD God of Israel than all the kings of Israel who were before him. During Ahab's reign, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho… in keeping with the LORD's message that he had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.”

eras.label: Era Sixteen · 1 Kings 17
eras.name: Elijah — the Drought and the Widow of Zarephath
eras.dates: Elijah enters the narrative without introduction, announces a drought by his own word, and is sustained first by ravens and then by a foreign widow whose flour and oil never run out.

events.title: "There Will Be No Dew or Rain"
events.detail: Elijah the Tishbite announces to Ahab that there will be no rain except at his word, then is sent by the LORD to hide by the Kerith Valley, where ravens bring him bread and meat until the stream dries up.

verses.text: “Elijah the Tishbite… said to Ahab, ‘As certainly as the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel lives, whom I stand before, there will be no dew or rain in the years ahead unless I give the command.’”

events.title: The Widow's Flour and Oil That Did Not Run Out
events.detail: Sent to a widow in Sidonian territory who has only enough for one last meal, Elijah promises her jar of flour and jug of oil will not run out until the drought ends — a promise that holds for the length of the famine.

verses.text: “This is what the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel has said: ‘The jar of flour will not be empty and the jug of oil will not run out until the day the LORD [Yahweh] makes it rain on the surface of the ground.’”

events.title: The Widow's Son Raised From Death
events.detail: When the widow's son stops breathing, Elijah carries him to the upper room, stretches over him three times, and cries out for his life to return — and it does, prompting the widow's confession that Elijah is truly a man of God whose word is truth.

verses.text: “He stretched himself over the boy three times and called out to the LORD [Yahweh] and said, ‘O LORD [Yahweh], my God [Elohim], let this boy's life return to him, please.’ And the LORD [Yahweh] listened to the voice of Elijah, and the boy's life returned to him and he lived.”

eras.label: Era Seventeen · 1 Kings 18
eras.name: The Contest on Mount Carmel
eras.dates: After three years of drought, Elijah confronts Ahab and 450 prophets of Baal in a single public test of which god can send fire — and, immediately after, prays down the rain his own word had withheld.

events.title: Obadiah, the Hidden Prophets, and Elijah's Return
events.detail: In the third year of the famine, Elijah reappears to Obadiah — Ahab's palace supervisor, who has secretly hidden a hundred of the LORD's prophets from Jezebel's purge in caves — and sends word ahead that he will present himself to Ahab that day.

verses.text: “Elijah said, ‘As certainly as the LORD [Yahweh] of Heaven's Armies lives, whom I stand before, I will present myself to him today.’”

events.title: "How Long Will You Waver Between Two Opinions?"
events.detail: Elijah confronts all Israel at Mount Carmel with a choice — the LORD or Baal — then proposes a public test: two bulls, two altars, no fire lit by human hands; the 450 prophets of Baal cry out, gash themselves, and dance from morning to evening with no response at all.

verses.text: “Elijah drew near to all the people and said, ‘How long will you be limping on the two crutches? If the LORD [Yahweh] is God [Elohim], walk after him, and if Baal, walk after him.’ And the people did not answer him a word.”

events.title: Fire Falls, and the People Cry "The LORD, He Is God!"
events.detail: Elijah repairs the LORD's ruined altar with twelve stones for the twelve tribes, drenches the sacrifice in water three times over, and prays a simple prayer — at which fire falls from the sky and consumes everything, sacrifice, wood, stones, and even the water in the trench, and the people fall on their faces confessing the LORD alone is God.

verses.text: “O LORD [Yahweh], God [Elohim] of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, this day let it be known that you are God [Elohim] in Israel and I am your servant… Answer me, O LORD [Yahweh], answer me, so that this people may know that you, O LORD [Yahweh], are God [Elohim].”
“And all the people saw it and they fell on their faces and said, ‘The LORD [Yahweh], he is God [Elohim]! The LORD [Yahweh], he is God [Elohim]!’”

events.title: The Cloud the Size of a Hand, and the Rain Returns
events.detail: Elijah tells Ahab to eat and drink because he hears the sound of coming rain, then bends to the ground in prayer while his servant checks the horizon seven times before spotting a cloud no bigger than a man's palm — the first sign of the drought's end, followed by a downpour so sudden Elijah outruns Ahab's chariot to Jezreel.

verses.text: “The seventh time the servant said, ‘Look, a small cloud, the size of the palm of a man's hand, is rising up from the sea.’”

eras.label: Era Eighteen · 1 Kings 19
eras.name: Elijah at Horeb — the Still, Small Voice
eras.dates: Jezebel's death threat sends Carmel's victorious prophet into suicidal despair within a single day, and the LORD answers not in wind, earthquake, or fire but in a soft whisper, followed by a fresh commission and a successor.

events.title: "I Have Had Enough"
events.detail: Terrified by Jezebel's vow to kill him within the day, Elijah flees into the wilderness and prays for death under a shrub, exhausted and alone — but an angel wakes him twice to eat, giving him strength for a forty-day journey to Horeb.

verses.text: “He went in the wilderness a day's journey and he came and sat under a broom tree, and he asked for himself to die, and he said, ‘Enough! Now, O LORD [Yahweh], take my life, for I am not better than my ancestors.’”

events.title: Wind, Earthquake, Fire, and Then a Soft Whisper
events.detail: At Horeb the LORD's question — "What are you doing here, Elijah?" — draws out the prophet's complaint of total isolation; the LORD passes by not in the wind that tears mountains, not in the earthquake, not in the fire, but in a still, small sound, after which Elijah repeats his complaint unchanged.

verses.text: “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD [Yahweh]… a wind great and strong was tearing out mountains before the LORD [Yahweh]; the LORD [Yahweh] was not in the wind. And after the wind an earthquake; the LORD [Yahweh] was not in the earthquake. And after the earthquake a fire; the LORD [Yahweh] was not in the fire. And after the fire, a sound of a soft whisper.”

events.title: A New Commission, and Seven Thousand Who Never Bowed
events.detail: The LORD sends Elijah back with three anointings to perform — Hazael over Syria, Jehu over Israel, and Elisha as his own prophetic successor — and corrects Elijah's despair with the fact that seven thousand in Israel have never bowed to Baal; Elisha responds by slaughtering his oxen and burning his plow to follow Elijah.

verses.text: “I will leave among Israel seven thousand — all the knees which have not bowed down to Baal, and every mouth which has not kissed him.”

eras.label: Era Nineteen · 1 Kings 20
eras.name: War With Ben Hadad
eras.dates: Syria's King Ben Hadad besieges Samaria with an overwhelming coalition, loses twice to a vastly smaller Israelite force by the LORD's own design, and is spared by Ahab in a mercy that a prophet condemns as disobedience.

events.title: Ben Hadad's Siege and Israel's Improbable Victory
events.detail: Ben Hadad of Syria besieges Samaria with thirty-two allied kings and escalating demands for Ahab's wives, sons, silver, and gold; a prophet promises the LORD will hand the huge army over to a small force of district-governors' servants, and Israel routs the drunken Syrian camp at noon.

verses.text: “A prophet visited King Ahab of Israel and said, ‘This is what the LORD has said: “Do you see this huge army? Look, I am going to hand it over to you this very day. Then you will know that I am the LORD.”’”

events.title: A Second Battle at Aphek, and Ben Hadad Spared
events.detail: Syria's advisers, convinced Israel's God is merely "a god of the mountains," attack again on flat ground at Aphek and lose again; Ben Hadad begs for his life, and Ahab — calling him "my brother" — releases him under a new treaty rather than executing him.

verses.text: “The advisers of the king of Syria said to him: ‘Their God is a god of the mountains. That's why they overpowered us. But if we fight them in the plains, we will certainly overpower them.’”

events.title: The Prophet's Parable of the Escaped Prisoner
events.detail: A member of the prophetic guild disguises himself and tricks Ahab into pronouncing judgment on himself for releasing a man the LORD had "determined should die" — a verdict Ahab receives "bitter and angry" rather than repentant.

verses.text: “The prophet then said to him, ‘This is what the LORD has said: “Because you released a man I had determined should die, you will pay with your life, and your people will suffer instead of his people.”’”

eras.label: Era Twenty · 1 Kings 21
eras.name: Naboth's Vineyard
eras.dates: Ahab's sulking over a vineyard he cannot buy gives Jezebel the opening to arrange a judicial murder, and Elijah meets the king at the very scene of the crime with the LORD's sentence on both of them.

events.title: Jezebel's Plot Against Naboth
events.detail: When Naboth refuses to sell his ancestral vineyard, citing the LORD's own command against alienating family inheritance, Ahab sulks in bed until Jezebel forges royal letters ordering false witnesses to accuse Naboth of cursing God and the king, resulting in his judicial stoning.

verses.text: “Naboth replied to Ahab, ‘Far be it from me, from the LORD [Yahweh], from giving my ancestral inheritance to you.’”

events.title: Elijah's Sentence, and Ahab's Delayed Judgment
events.detail: Elijah meets Ahab at the seized vineyard with a sentence for both king and queen — dogs will lick Ahab's blood where they licked Naboth's, and dogs will devour Jezebel by Jezreel's wall; Ahab's visible remorse, tearing his clothes and fasting, moves the LORD to delay the disaster until his son's reign.

verses.text: “You will speak to him: thus says the LORD [Yahweh], ‘Have you murdered, and also taken possession?’ … ‘In the place where the dogs lapped up the blood of Naboth, the dogs will lap up your blood also, you.’”
“Have you seen that Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the evil in his days; in the days of his son I will bring the evil on his house.”

eras.label: Era Twenty-One · 1 Kings 22
eras.name: Micaiah, the Death of Ahab, and Jehoshaphat's Reign
eras.dates: Four hundred court prophets promise Ahab victory at Ramoth Gilead; the one true prophet, Micaiah, describes the deceiving spirit sent to lure the king to his death — and is proven right by a single stray arrow.

events.title: Four Hundred Prophets, and One Who Tells the Truth
events.detail: Allied with King Jehoshaphat of Judah, Ahab consults 400 court prophets who unanimously predict victory at Ramoth Gilead; summoned against his handler's advice to agree with the majority, Micaiah instead describes Israel "scattered on the mountains like sheep that have no shepherd" — a vision of defeat and a leaderless army.

verses.text: “Micaiah said, ‘I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep that have no shepherd. Then the LORD said, “They have no master. They should go home in peace.”’”

events.title: The Deceiving Spirit in the Heavenly Court
events.detail: Pressed further, Micaiah describes a throne-room vision: the LORD asking who will entice Ahab to his death, and a spirit volunteering to be "a lying spirit" in the mouths of all of Ahab's prophets — meaning the 400 unanimous voices of victory are themselves the instrument of Ahab's coming destruction.

verses.text: “I saw the LORD [Yahweh] sitting on his throne, with all the heavenly assembly standing beside him… A spirit stepped forward and stood before the LORD [Yahweh]. He said, ‘I will deceive him.’ … ‘I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ … So now, look, the LORD [Yahweh] has placed a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours, but the LORD [Yahweh] has decreed disaster for you.”

events.title: The Disguised King and the Random Arrow
events.detail: Ahab enters battle disguised while Jehoshaphat wears royal robes, yet an archer's arrow "shot at random" finds the gap in Ahab's armor anyway; he bleeds to death propped up in his chariot through the day, and dogs lick his blood at the pool of Samaria exactly as Elijah had foretold.

verses.text: “Now an archer shot an arrow at random, and it struck the king of Israel between the plates of his armor.”
“They washed off the chariot at the pool of Samaria. Then the dogs licked his blood… in keeping with the LORD's message that he had spoken.”

events.title: Jehoshaphat's Reign; Ahaziah Begins in Israel
events.detail: Jehoshaphat reigns twenty-five years in Jerusalem, following his father Asa's example though the high places remain, and builds a merchant fleet that wrecks before ever sailing; the book closes with Ahab's son Ahaziah beginning his own two-year reign in Israel, following his parents' worship of Baal. (Verses 43-44 numbered 22:44-45 in most English translations, due to a Hebrew versification shift late in the chapter.)

verses.text: “He worshiped and bowed down to Baal, angering the LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Israel just as his father had done.” (Numbered 22:53 in most English translations; 22:54 in Hebrew numbering.)
